analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by trusting an attacker-controlled dictionary length from chunk data after narrowing it to int32_t for bounds checks, then using the original size_t value for ZSTD_createDDict(). In initialize_context_decompression(), dict_size is read from frame bytes and checked with `if (srcsize < (int32_t)context->dict_size)`, which can overflow/truncate when dict_size > INT32_MAX. The check can pass incorrectly, but then `ZSTD_createDDict(context->dict_buffer, context->dict_size)` copies `dict_size` bytes (by memcpy in ZSTD_initDDict_internal), reading past the provided input buffer.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In decompress_frame_fuzzer, attacker-controlled frame/chunk bytes reach frame_decompress_chunk() -> blosc2_decompress_ctx() -> initialize_context_decompression(). The chunk must set BLOSC2_USEDICT and encode a large dictionary size value (via sw32_ field) such that cast to int32_t breaks the `srcsize` comparison, while remaining <= BLOSC2_MAXDICTSIZE. Then dict_buffer points into the input, and ZSTD_createDDict() performs an oversized memcpy from that pointer, triggering heap-buffer-overflow read.
